name: Death: EXP penalty and respawn

death_trigger.statement: You'll die when your HP reaches 0, so it's for your own good to consume a potion or food before it's too late.

exp_penalty.status: MeowDB's Model (MeowDB's own model of the mechanic; not a confirmed game constant)
formulas: Loss = floor(EXP to next level × (5 + 20 / LUK) / 100)
EXP after death = max(0, EXP - Loss)
notes: LUK is base LUK: the points you put in, before gear.
EXP stops at 0, so a death never takes away a level.
A Safety Charm stops the loss.
exp_penalty.luk_basis: The character's own base LUK: the starting 4 plus every AP placed in LUK, before equipment and buffs ("the points you put in, before gear"). Every character starts with 4 LUK, and MeowDB's calculator clamps the input to 4..999. Do not use only the allocated AP (that can be 0 and would divide by zero).
exp_penalty.exceptions_note: MeowDB documents NO exception for dying in town and NO Beginner exception. The only documented way to avoid the loss is a Safety Charm. Do not add exceptions from other sources without recording them as external.

respawn_location.rule: Each map has a "Respawn Map" ("Where you return after dying") on its MeowDB map page; use the maps domain value.

example.text: Respawn Map Southperry Where you return after dying

general_statement: Combat is slower. Monsters can take several hits, potions matter, maps are crossed on foot, and death costs EXP.
gaps: HP/MP after respawning is not documented.
Respawn delay / death screen timing is not documented.
Whether items or mesos are lost on death is not documented (only EXP loss is).
Town or Beginner exceptions to the EXP loss are not documented (none listed).
